Companion page: Shift Baselines (the follow-on baselines on the same households).

The mixture starts the week with a library of competing weekly models of the home, written from one walkthrough and the residents' intro cards. Each patrol pass re-weights the library; when the evidence goes against a document's claims, the writer is asked to add documents. This page shows which documents carry the belief, how their weights move through the weekend and the event days, and whether being told about a shift changes anything.

Protocol: nightly patrol at 03:00 + found-it feedback (the robot learns where the object turned out to be 10 min after each question). Updated 21 Sep 05:03. Run v4 (02:02): likelihood floor 1e-3, recency term (4 h half-life) in the documents, share-cap entry for revised documents. Told arms: hh_s11 and hh_s14 finished their week (ESS 7-10 throughout, no collapses); hh_s10 on Tuesday; hh_s18/s19 through Saturday; hh_s25 through Friday; not-told arms follow each group (identical before the first message day, replayed from cache), then hh_s12/s13. Read so far: on questions whose object moved since the round the mixture tracks the timetable (Wed 8-27%, Fri 26-30%) at confidence 0.22-0.34; on the households' own shift days the timetable's confident half falls 16 points at unchanged confidence, the mixture's falls 6 and stays the best of any agent; no agent lowers its mean confidence on shift days; on the still half the mixture loses to last seen on shift mornings (routine predictions at in-use spots). Reference lines are the classical logs on the same protocol; the naive LLM line is built from its call log. Overnight log: results/confidence_shift_2026-09-20/overnight_status.md.

How sure it was, day by day

Accuracy on all questions; the mixture's probability on its own answer (what it would state as confidence); the share of the library's weight whose own answer agrees (confidence from the weighting: 100% = every document that matters says the same spot); share of answers at probability ≥ 0.7; and the effective number of documents carrying the mixture (1 = one document has taken over). The reference lines are the most-frequent counter and the naive LLM on the same questions.

Every question across the week, left to right; each band is one document's weight. Vertical rules are day boundaries; shaded days are shift days; a ◆ marks a revision (documents added). Hover a band to see the document.

Told minus not told
